answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive — like trying to fill an ocean one cup at a time. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work, like a falcon earning trust flight by flight, rather than being granted at registration. At its nadir, a new identity has zero reputation and minimal permissions, so even a flood of fresh fakes cannot outvote established agents or drain shared treasuries.
